parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` (line 34, MP3Streamer target) and `TimeShiftablePlayer` (line 20, PlaybackCore target) share surface-level member names such as `installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, and `stop:()`, the pipeline itself reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, reflecting that no fields match exactly. Key divergences confirm distinct abstraction layers: `play` carries a `throws` specifier only on `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol`; `eventStream` is typed `AsyncStream<AudioPlayerEvent>` vs `AsyncStream<AudioPlayerInternalEvent>`; and `TimeShiftablePlayer` adds an entirely separate concern (`seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `isAtLiveEdge`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`) that has no counterpart in `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol`. Introducing a shared parent protocol would require either weakening the `play` contract or erasing the event-type distinction, coupling two independently evolving abstraction layers without a genuine semantic hierarchy to justify it.
